div.div: How an agent's identity reaches the AI Gateway

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 43px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Entra ID does three different jobs here, on three different clocks. Cloud Identity Engine does one of them. Separating them is most of the answer.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 290px; height: 1px; padding-top: 95px; margin-left: 13px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
There is no User-ID here.
User-ID is a PAN-OS mechanism. The firewall learns an IP-to-user mapping out of band, from a domain controller or an agent, and security policy then matches on the user it found.
The AI Gateway has none of that. No IP-to-user mapping, no User-ID agent, and no directory group travelling on the request.
Identity arrives inside the request, as the credential itself.
So the question to ask is not "how do I turn on User-ID". It is which credential does the agent present, and what identity does that credential carry.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 409px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: The three jobs Entra ID does

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 290px; height: 1px; padding-top: 437px; margin-left: 13px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1. Source directory, behind CIE.
Supplies the users and groups that become workspace membership. Runs on a sync schedule, not per request.
2. Token issuer for the agent.
Signs the JWT the agent presents. The gateway validates it against Entra's JWKS. This is per request.
3. Egress credential to Azure.
A service principal or managed identity the gateway uses to reach Azure AI Foundry. Nothing to do with the caller.
All three can be the same Entra tenant. They are still three separate configurations.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 767px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: What each credential attributes to

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 290px; height: 1px; padding-top: 795px; margin-left: 13px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Service API key
Shared, not tied to a person. The request attributes to the application. Split further only with metadata you set yourself.
User API key
Tied to one directory-provisioned member. The user picker only lists people CIE has already synced into that workspace.
JWT from your IdP
The gateway reads identity from the claims, in this precedence order:
email_id → sub → uid

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;

div.div: Which one an agent should use

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 498px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1225px; margin-left: 13px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Unattended, no human behind it — a Service API key per agent, with metadata naming the agent. There is no person to attribute to, so do not pretend there is one.
Acting for a signed-in person — a JWT carrying that person's email. Attribution and the workspace role both follow the human.
A named service account you want in the member list — a User API key issued against a CIE-provisioned user.

div.div: 1 · CONTROL PLANE — who belongs to which workspace

Entra ID
Your directory of users and groups.
Okta and on-prem AD sit here too.

div.div:
Cloud Identity Engine
Aggregates and caches the directories you connect.
SCM → Cloud Identity Engine → Directory Sync

div.div:
Directory Sync
Pick the Connected Directory and the User Identity Attribute: UPN or Mail.
AI Gateway → Admin Settings → Authentication

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 218px; height: 1px; padding-top: 139px; margin-left: 1155px;

div.div:
Group → Workspace
A 1:1 mapping. One group to one workspace, one workspace to one group.
The workspace must already exist.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 218px; height: 1px; padding-top: 139px; margin-left: 1415px;

div.div:
Workspace members
Provisioned and deprovisioned for you as group membership changes.
This list is what a User API key can be issued against.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1298px; height: 1px; padding-top: 271px; margin-left: 367px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Timing — delta sync every 15 minutes, so a group change takes up to 15 minutes to land. CIE rebuilds its cache roughly weekly and the gateway full-syncs automatically; Full Sync forces it. • Scope — CIE Directory Sync is for SCM tenants. A non-SCM deployment uses SCIM provisioning instead.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1322px; height: 1px; padding-top: 375px; margin-left: 357px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Where the two halves meet, and the one string that has to match
When the email on the agent's token matches an AI Gateway user in the target workspace, the request is attributed to that person and inherits their workspace role. When it does not match, the request falls back to a generic workspace service key and the per-user attribution is lost.
That comparison is a plain string match. The User Identity Attribute you chose in Directory Sync (UPN or Mail) has to produce the same value as the email claim Entra puts in the token. Choose Mail when the UPN is user@tenant.onmicrosoft.com but the real address is not.

div.div:
The agent
A workload, not a person at a browser. It holds a client ID and a secret, or a managed identity.
Registered as an app in the Azure portal.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 194px; height: 1px; padding-top: 581px; margin-left: 615px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Entra ID issues a token
Signed RS256, carrying iss, aud, sub, exp, and an email claim.
Sent to the gateway as Authorization: Bearer, or in x-portkey-api-key.
The gateway never sees the agent's secret.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 575px; margin-left: 863px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;

div.div: Prisma AIRS AI Gateway

div.div:
Validate
Signature against the JWKS, kid match, exp in the future.
JWKS: the Entra discovery/v2.0/keys endpoint for your tenant.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 176px; height: 1px; padding-top: 606px; margin-left: 1072px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Resolve org and workspace
Org: portkey_oid → organisation_id → the single org in ORGANISATIONS_TO_SYNC.
Workspace: portkey_workspace → workspace_slug → deployment default.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 176px; height: 1px; padding-top: 606px; margin-left: 1274px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Check scope
Each route needs its own scope:
completions.write for chat
agents.invoke for agents
mcp.invoke for MCP
Missing scope returns 403.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 176px; height: 1px; padding-top: 606px; margin-left: 1476px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Attribute the request
Identity taken from email_id, then sub, then uid.
Then budgets, rate limits and policies apply, exactly as they would for an API key.
This is what lands in the logs.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1298px; height: 1px; padding-top: 833px; margin-left: 367px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Where validation runs — on AI Gateway Cloud the management plane validates the token. A hybrid or air-gapped gateway can validate locally with JWT_ENABLED=ON on gateway 2.5.0 or later, which keeps authentication working when the management plane is unreachable. • Mode A is for when you control the token issuer and can add the gateway's own claims. Mode B is the Entra case: a stock IdP token, with org, workspace and scopes resolved on the gateway instead. Use JWT_LOCAL_AUTH_DEFAULT_SCOPES when you cannot add scopes in Entra. • Entra values — JWKS login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/discovery/v2.0/keys, issuer login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0, audience {client-id}.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 959px; margin-left: 365px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: 3 · EGRESS — how the gateway reaches the provider

div.div:
AI Gateway
Swaps the caller's credential for the provider's.
Two independent layers.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 218px; height: 1px; padding-top: 997px; margin-left: 675px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Azure AI Foundry
or Azure OpenAI
In your own subscription, billed on your own meter.
Role on the resource:
Cognitive Services OpenAI User

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 662px; height: 1px; padding-top: 989px; margin-left: 999px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The three auth types the integration form accepts
Resource API key — the static secret. Simplest, and the one to move away from.
Azure Managed Entity — a managed identity plus its Managed ClientID. No secret to store.
Azure Entra ID — ClientID, Secret and Tenant ID for a service principal.
Keyless is possible on the Azure side. The static resource key is a choice, not a requirement.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1298px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1129px; margin-left: 367px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The agent authenticates to the gateway. The gateway authenticates to Azure. Neither credential is ever visible to the other side, which is the whole point of putting the gateway in the path.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1195px; margin-left: 547px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Six things that silently break this

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1122px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1225px; margin-left: 557px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1. RS256 only. An HS256 token is rejected, and the error reads as a bad API key rather than a bad algorithm. • 2. The kid in the token header must match a key in the configured JWKS. • 3. exp is mandatory; a token without one never authenticates.
4. A user whose chosen identity attribute is empty in CIE is skipped during sync, with no error on the request that later fails to attribute. • 5. Deleting a group mapping removes those users from the workspace immediately, and the mapping does not come back by re-enabling sync. • 6. On a multi-org gateway a token with no org claim is rejected with a 401; set a single org in ORGANISATIONS_TO_SYNC or add portkey_oid to the token.
